questions.q: Which of the following represents de Broglie equation?
questions.explanation: The de Broglie wavelength is $\lambda = h/mv = h/p$, matching option B.

questions.q: Which of the following is the CORRECT statement about $\Psi^2$?
options: Probability density of the electron at that point
questions.explanation: $\Psi^2$ gives the probability density of finding the electron at a given point in space; at nodes $\Psi^2 = 0$.

questions.q: The number of orbitals associated with 'N' shell of an atom is
questions.explanation: The N shell has principal quantum number n=4, and the total number of orbitals in a shell is n$^2$ = 16.

questions.q: According to the Heisenberg's Uncertainty principle, the value of $\Delta v.\Delta x$ for an object whose mass is 10$^{-6}$kg is (h = 6.626×10$^{-34}$Js)
questions.explanation: $\Delta v.\Delta x \ge \dfrac{h}{4\pi m} = \dfrac{6.626\times10^{-34}}{4\pi\times10^{-6}} \approx 5.2\times10^{-29}$ (SI units).

questions.q: The energy associated with the first orbit of He$^+$ is:
The number of protons, neutrons and electrons in the ion $^{32}_{16}$S$^{2-}$ respectively are
questions.explanation: Protons = atomic number = 16; neutrons = 32-16 = 16; electrons = 16 + 2 (for the 2- charge) = 18.

questions.q: If wavelength of photon is 2.2 $\times$ 10$^{-11}$ m and h = 6.6 $\times$ 10$^{-34}$ J s, then momentum of photon
The number of angular and radial nodes in 3p orbital respectively are
questions.explanation: Angular nodes = l = 1 for a p orbital; radial nodes = n − l − 1 = 3 − 1 − 1 = 1.

questions.q: With regard to photoelectric effect, identify the CORRECT statement among the following:
options: Number of e$^-$ ejected increases with the increase in the intensity of incident light.
Energy of e$^-$ ejected increases with the increase in the intensity of incident light.
Number of e$^-$ ejected increases with the increase in the frequency of incident light.
Number of e$^-$ ejected increases with the increase in work function.
questions.explanation: In the photoelectric effect, the number of photoelectrons ejected depends on the intensity of light, while their kinetic energy depends on the frequency, not the intensity.

questions.q: Two particles A and B are in motion. If the wavelength associated with 'A' is 33.33 nm, the wavelength associated with 'B' whose momentum is $\dfrac{1}{3}$rd of 'A' is
questions.explanation: Since $\lambda = h/p$, if $p_B = p_A/3$ then $\lambda_B = 3\lambda_A = 3 \times 33.33$ nm $\approx 1.0\times10^{-7}$ m.

questions.q: The orbital nearest to the nucleus is
questions.explanation: By the (n+l) rule, 4s has (n+l)=4, the lowest among the given orbitals, so it is filled first and lies nearest/lowest in energy.

questions.q: The correct set of quantum number for the unpaired electrons of chlorine atom is
questions.explanation: Cl has configuration [Ne]3s$^2$3p$^5$; its unpaired electron lies in a 3p orbital, so n=3, l=1, m=+1 (or -1), s=$\pm\dfrac{1}{2}$, matching option C.

questions.q: The energy of electron in the n$^{th}$ Bohr orbit of H-atom is
questions.explanation: For a hydrogen atom, the energy of the electron in the n$^{th}$ Bohr orbit is $E_n = -13.6/n^2$ eV.

questions.q: Consider the following sets of quantum numbers : Which of the below setting is not permissible arrangement of electrons in an atom ?
questions.explanation: For l=2, the magnetic quantum number m can only range from $-2$ to $+2$; m=$-3$ is not allowed, making option (4) impermissible.

questions.q: The two electrons have the following set of quantum numbers : P = 3, 2, -2, +$\dfrac{1}{2}$ ; Q = 3, 0, 0, +$\dfrac{1}{2}$. Which of the following statement is true?
options: P and Q have same energy
P has greater energy than Q
P has lesser energy than Q
P and Q represent same electron
questions.explanation: P (n=3, l=2) is a 3d electron and Q (n=3, l=0) is a 3s electron; using the (n+l) rule, 3d (n+l=5) has higher energy than 3s (n+l=3), so P has greater energy than Q.

questions.q: Among the elements from atomic number 1 to 36, the number of elements which have an unpaired electron in their s subshell is
questions.explanation: Elements with an unpaired s-electron (outermost ns$^1$ configuration, ignoring completely filled cases) from Z=1 to 36 are H, Li, Na, K, Cr (4s$^1$), Cu (4s$^1$) — 6 elements in total.

questions.q: The statement that is NOT correct is
options: The radius of the first orbit of He$^+$ is half that of the first orbit of hydrogen atom.
Total number of nodes for 3s orbital is three.
Energies of stationary states in hydrogen like atoms is inversely proportional to the square of the principal quantum number.
Angular quantum number signifies the shape of the orbital.
questions.explanation: The 3s orbital has (n-1) = 2 total nodes, not three (2 radial nodes, 0 angular nodes), so statement (2) is incorrect.

questions.q: Impossible orbital among the following is
questions.explanation: For n=3, l can be 0,1,2 (s,p,d) only; f (l=3) requires n≥4, so 3f cannot exist.

questions.q: The correct set of four quantum numbers for the outermost electron of sodium (Z = 11) is
questions.explanation: Sodium's outermost electron is in 3s$^1$: n=3, l=0 (s-orbital), m=0, s=+½.

questions.q: Which one of the following sets of quantum numbers represents the highest energy level in an atom?
questions.explanation: Using the (n+l) rule, option 3 (3d) has n+l=5, higher than 4s(4), 3p(4) and 3s(3), so it represents the highest energy level.

questions.q: If the energies of the two photons are in the ratio of 3 : 2, their wavelengths will be in the ratio of .....................
questions.explanation: Since $E=\dfrac{hc}{\lambda}$, wavelength is inversely proportional to energy, so the wavelength ratio is the inverse of the energy ratio, i.e. 2 : 3.

questions.q: The wave number of the spectral line in the emission spectrum of hydrogen will be equal to $\dfrac{8}{9}$ times the Rydberg's constant if the electron jumps from .......................
questions.explanation: $\bar\nu = R\left(\dfrac{1}{1^2}-\dfrac{1}{3^2}\right) = R\left(1-\dfrac{1}{9}\right) = \dfrac{8}{9}R$, so the transition is n=3 to n=1.

questions.q: The set of quantum numbers for the outermost electron for copper in its ground state is.......................
questions.explanation: Cu is [Ar]3d$^{10}$4s$^1$; the outermost electron is in 4s, giving n=4, l=0, m=0, s=+1/2.

questions.q: The correct set of four Quantum numbers for outermost electron of Potassium (Z = 19) is
questions.explanation: K has configuration [Ar]4s$^1$, so the outermost electron has n=4, l=0, m=0, s=+1/2.

questions.q: A body of mass x kg is moving with a velocity of 100 ms$^{-1}$. Its de Broglie wavelength is $6.62 \times 10^{-35}$m. Hence x is (h = $6.62 \times 10^{-34}$ Js)
questions.explanation: $\lambda = h/(mv) \Rightarrow m = h/(\lambda v) = 6.62\times10^{-34}/(6.62\times10^{-35}\times100) = 0.1$ kg.
